facts: A discrimination and robustness oriented adaptive learning procedure is proposed.
The proposed adaptive learning procedure deals with the task of syntactic ambiguity resolution.
Insufficient training data is a problem.
Approximation error is introduced by the language model.
Traditional statistical approaches resolve ambiguities by indirectly and implicitly using maximum likelihood method.
Traditional statistical approaches fail to achieve high performance in real applications.
The proposed method remedies problems by adjusting the parameters.
The proposed method maximizes the accuracy rate directly.
Possible variations between the training corpus and the real tasks are taken into consideration.
The separation margin between the correct candidate and its competing members is enlarged.
Enlarging the separation margin between the correct candidate and its competing members is intended to make the proposed algorithm robust.
Significant improvement has been observed in the test.
Using the novel approach raises the accuracy rate of syntactic disambiguation from 46.0% to 60.62%.
The accuracy rate before using the novel approach is 46.0%.
The accuracy rate after using the novel approach is 60.62%.
